class_id: a test's git fixture runs in the host repository because an inherited GIT_DIR (or a failed cd) points git back at it
feature: any test (shell or node) that builds a throwaway git repository with git init / config / add / commit, especially one run by a git hook (pre-commit, pre-push) inside a real checkout
symptom: the fixture creates a temp directory and runs git init, git config user.*, writes files and commits there. Two ways git ends up operating on the CALLER's repository instead: (1) the test runs under a git hook, and git exports GIT_DIR to hooks (in a push from a linked worktree GIT_DIR=.git/worktrees/<name>); an exported GIT_DIR wins over both `cd <tmp>` and `git -C <tmp>`, so every fixture command targets the real repo, and `git init` under a foreign GIT_DIR rewrites its config (core.bare=true) -- this was the measured mechanism; (2) a `( cd "$tmp"; git ... )` whose cd fails without stopping. Its shared .git/config gains the fixture's identity (and core.bare when the fixture initialises a bare repo), fixture files overwrite real files, and fixture commits land on the real branch. In a linked worktree the damage spreads, because every worktree shares the main checkout's config: one bad run broke git for every checkout of the repo at once. A test run by a hook makes it worse: the developer never chose to run it.
